# OCD & Anxiety Counselling Vancouver | Unravel

Unravel Counselling offers individual online OCD and anxiety counselling for adults in Vancouver and across British Columbia.

## Care and practical details

Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is the main therapeutic framework. Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) is used for OCD. EMDR is a secondary approach for anxiety and trauma where appropriate. Theekshitha Vadladi is a mental health counsellor who has completed all requirements for a master’s in Counselling Psychology. Clients must be aged 18+ and physically in BC during sessions. Individual sessions are CAD $145 for 50 minutes or CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. A free 15-minute consultation is available by phone or video.

# Online OCD Therapy Vancouver | Unravel Counselling

Individual virtual OCD counselling for adults in Vancouver and across British Columbia, with OCD-specific ERP within an ACT-led framework.

## When doubt starts deciding how you spend your day.

Checking once more. Replaying a conversation. Searching for an answer that finally feels certain. OCD can take hours without anyone else seeing what is happening. The difficulty is often less about the subject of a thought than the repeated demands that follow it.

Unravel offers virtual OCD therapy with [Theekshitha Vadladi](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/), for adults aged 18 and over who are physically in BC during sessions. The work focuses on understanding the pattern, reducing the rituals that sustain it and reconnecting treatment with the things you want to take part in.

## OCD is more than being careful or organised.

Obsessive-compulsive disorder can involve recurring obsessions, compulsions, or both. Obsessions are unwanted thoughts, images or urges. Compulsions are repetitive behaviours or mental acts that someone feels driven to perform, often to reduce distress or prevent a feared outcome. OCD symptoms can become time-consuming and interfere with ordinary activities. [NIMH explains the symptoms and assessment of OCD.](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over)

Compulsions may be visible, such as washing or checking, or internal, such as mentally reviewing, repeating words or testing a feeling. Asking others for reassurance can also become part of the pattern. The brief relief may be followed by another question, another check or another attempt to settle the doubt.

Having an intrusive thought or a particular habit does not by itself establish OCD. Counselling considers the wider pattern, its purpose and its effect on your life. The [guide to OCD themes and intrusive thoughts](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-types/) introduces common terms without asking you to diagnose yourself.

For a closer look at internal rituals, read [mental compulsions in OCD](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/mental-compulsions-ocd/).

## ERP addresses the cycle. ACT connects it with your life.

[Exposure and Response Prevention](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/) is a form of cognitive behavioural therapy and a first-line psychological treatment for OCD. It pairs planned contact with triggers with practice changing the compulsive response. This includes attention to mental rituals and avoidance, not simply doing something that feels frightening. [The IOCDF describes how ERP works.](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/)

[Acceptance and Commitment Therapy](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/) is Unravel’s main therapeutic framework. In OCD care, ACT supports willingness, attention and action guided by your values alongside ERP. These approaches have different roles: ACT does not replace the OCD-specific response-prevention work.

For example, a goal might be spending an evening with family without losing most of it to mental checking. That goal gives practice a purpose and helps shape a plan suited to your needs, circumstances and readiness.

## Your beliefs and relationships are part of the context.

OCD may attach to things that matter deeply: responsibility, faith, relationships or being a good person. Understanding those commitments comes before deciding what a compulsive response looks like. A valued religious or cultural practice should not be treated as a symptom simply because it is unfamiliar. [The IOCDF offers guidance on religiously sensitive ERP.](https://iocdf.org/faith-ocd/mental-health-providers/principles-of-effective-and-religiously-sensitive-exposures/)

Unravel brings an understanding of South Asian and first-generation experiences while welcoming adults from all backgrounds. Shared identity does not mean identical experiences. Family expectations, privacy, belonging and the cost of asking for help deserve attention alongside the OCD pattern.

## OCD counselling for Vancouver, delivered online.

Vancouver clients attend virtually, as do clients elsewhere in British Columbia. A private place to speak, a suitable device and a workable internet connection help make the online setting useful. Clients must be physically located in BC at the time of care.

Choosing an OCD therapist also means checking the person’s actual training and approach. Theekshitha’s education and completed ERP course are listed on the [counsellor page](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/). The [IOCDF’s therapist-selection guide](https://iocdf.org/ocd-finding-help/how-to-find-the-right-therapist/) provides questions about OCD-specific methods, training and cultural context.

## What beginning OCD counselling involves.

### Start with a consultation

A free 15-minute phone or video consultation covers the approach, availability and practical questions. It is a chance to consider working together before arranging paid sessions.

### Understand the pattern

Early sessions explore what triggers the cycle, the responses that follow and the activities OCD is interrupting. Your goals help guide the treatment plan.

### Practise and review

Where ERP is appropriate, agree on practice and review what happens. Obstacles, internal rituals and the effect on daily life remain part of the work.

## Fees and format

Free consultation: 15 minutes, phone or video. Individual session: CAD $145 for 50 minutes. Extended individual session: CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. Adults 18+, virtual, physically located in BC during sessions.

## Common questions

### Do I need a diagnosis before contacting Unravel?

No confirmed diagnosis is required to enquire. Describe what is happening and how it affects you. The consultation explores fit and next steps; it is not a formal diagnostic assessment or a diagnostic report.

### Can OCD counselling address mental compulsions?

Yes. Mental reviewing, repeated internal phrases and other rituals can be relevant to the response-prevention plan. Their function and context matter; ordinary thinking is not automatically a compulsion.

### Is OCD therapy available in person in Vancouver?

Unravel’s sessions are virtual. Adults in Vancouver and elsewhere in BC meet online and must be physically located in British Columbia during sessions.

### How long does OCD treatment take?

There is no fixed course or outcome promised. Goals, session frequency, affordability and response to the work inform the plan and should be reviewed as counselling continues.

# ERP Therapy Vancouver & BC | Unravel Counselling

Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) for OCD, offered within virtual individual counselling for adults in Vancouver and across BC.

## The two parts work together.

Exposure means approaching a planned situation, thought or other trigger associated with OCD-related distress. Response prevention means practising without the ritual or other compulsive response that usually follows. ERP is a form of cognitive behavioural therapy and a first-line psychological treatment for OCD. [Read the IOCDF’s ERP overview.](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/)

ERP is not simply a challenge to face the scariest thing on a list. It involves understanding the pattern, agreeing on the purpose of practice and paying attention to what happens before, during and after it. At Unravel, ACT is the main framework; ERP provides the OCD-specific behavioural work within that approach.

## Notice the ritual as well as the trigger.

Compulsive responses may involve washing, checking, asking for reassurance, mentally reviewing or attempting to neutralise a thought. Avoidance can also shape the cycle. If an exposure is followed by a less visible ritual, the response-prevention part still needs attention. [NICE includes mental rituals and neutralising strategies in its OCD treatment recommendations.](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg31/chapter/Recommendations)

For example, someone may appear to have finished an agreed practice while continuing to replay it mentally afterwards. That is useful information for understanding the pattern, rather than a reason to call the attempt a failure. Repeated reasoning can be part of a compulsion when it serves the demand for certainty.

Response prevention does not mean forcing your mind to become blank or treating every difficult thought as a problem. The focus is the response that keeps the OCD cycle going. Identifying it accurately matters more than how an exercise looks from the outside.

The article on [rumination and OCD](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/rumination-ocd/) explains how repeated reviewing can become part of the cycle.

## A clear plan, with your participation.

ERP commonly begins with education about OCD, identifying triggers and responses, and building a list of practice opportunities. Exposures may involve real situations or imagined scenarios. They are planned with your participation; you should not be deceived or forced into them. [The IOCDF outlines this process.](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/)

The plan needs to distinguish a chosen practice from an ordinary responsibility or genuine health and safety concern. Your circumstances, beliefs and readiness belong in that judgement. The purpose of a step, the response being addressed and the difficulties it may raise should be understandable.

ERP can involve distress and uncertainty. The aim is not to prove that a feared event can never happen or to promise that anxiety will disappear during every exercise. Practice is reviewed in relation to the pattern and the life it interrupts.

## Practice needs a reason beyond completing an exercise.

At Unravel, [ACT](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/) helps connect ERP with values and the way you respond to thoughts and feelings. A meaningful direction might concern a relationship, work, rest or a valued activity. Those priorities come from the individual rather than a standard set of goals.

The [IOCDF treatment guide](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/) describes ACT as an adjunctive approach in OCD care. Its role at Unravel is to support the willingness and direction involved in the work, while ERP addresses compulsive responding.

Progress deserves a broader view than whether a practice felt easy. Changes in time spent on rituals, participation in daily activities and responses to uncertainty can all be relevant to reviewing your goals. Goals and progress are reviewed throughout the work.

Completed training: 4-Day Intensive Workshop: Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy for OCD, Cognitive Behavior Institute (CBI Center for Education), with Alissa Jerud, PhD.

## ERP in an online setting.

Virtual ERP at Unravel is available to adults aged 18 and over who are physically in British Columbia during sessions. Vancouver clients meet online. The online setting needs to support private communication and the practice that has been agreed.

Between-session practice is commonly part of ERP. What is proposed should be clear and realistic alongside your responsibilities. Appointments provide time to review what was attempted, what got in the way and what was learned. The free consultation covers practical arrangements; it does not provide an individual exposure plan.

[The OCD counselling page](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/) explains the wider care pathway. The [counsellor profile](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/) sets out Theekshitha Vadladi’s education and completed training.

## From understanding the cycle to reviewing practice.

### Map the pattern

Identify the trigger, the visible or mental response, and the effect on daily life. Establish what the work is intended to help you return to.

### Agree on a starting point

Clarify the purpose of practice and the compulsive response being addressed. Questions, practical limits and willingness are part of planning.

### Learn from what happens

Review practice, including difficulties and less visible rituals. Use that information to refine the next step rather than measuring success only by comfort.

## Fees and format

Free consultation: 15 minutes, phone or video. Individual session: CAD $145 for 50 minutes. Extended individual session: CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. Adults 18+, virtual, physically located in BC during sessions.

## Common questions

### Is ERP a type of CBT?

Yes. Exposure and Response Prevention is a form of cognitive behavioural therapy developed for OCD-related patterns. It combines exposure with attention to compulsions, including mental rituals.

### Can ERP be used for mental compulsions?

Yes. Mental reviewing, neutralising and other internal rituals can be addressed within response prevention. The plan considers what the thinking is doing in the cycle rather than labelling all thought as a ritual.

### Does ERP involve being forced into an exposure?

No. The purpose and difficulties of a proposed step should be explained, and practice is planned with your participation. Feeling challenged and being coerced are different experiences.

### What does ERP cost at Unravel?

ERP is offered within individual counselling: CAD $145 for 50 minutes or CAD $190 for a 90-minute extended session. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. See [fees and session options](https://unravelcounselling.com/low-cost-counselling-bc/).

## Where to next

- [The OCD care pathway](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/)
- [Acceptance and Commitment Therapy](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/)
- [Education and ERP training](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)
- [Book a free consultation](https://unravelcounselling.janeapp.com/#staff_member/1)
- [Rumination and OCD](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/rumination-ocd/)

# Anxiety Counselling Vancouver | Online at Unravel

Online anxiety counselling for adults in Vancouver and throughout British Columbia. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy is the main approach.

## Anxiety can be exhausting even when you seem to be coping.

Perhaps you get through work while repeatedly preparing for what might go wrong. Or a small decision takes an evening because none of the options feels safe enough. These are examples of how anxiety may affect a day, not a test of whether you have a particular disorder.

Counselling starts with the effect on your life: what anxiety pulls you away from, the responses you rely on and what you want to be different. Unravel works with adults in Vancouver and throughout BC. Sessions are individual and online, with attention to your values and the circumstances you are living in.

## Look at the pattern and its cost.

Anxiety can include persistent worry, feeling on edge, muscle tension, disrupted sleep and difficulty concentrating. Occasional anxiety is common; ongoing distress that interferes with daily activities deserves attention. Symptoms alone do not establish a diagnosis. [NIMH explains anxiety symptoms and the role of assessment.](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/generalized-anxiety-disorder-gad)

The effects are not always obvious. Someone may keep meeting responsibilities while spending much of their time anticipating problems, avoiding decisions or trying to settle every possible uncertainty. The effort involved matters, even when others do not see it.

Work demands, financial strain, discrimination, migration and family expectations may be real pressures. Therapy should consider those conditions alongside your responses to anxiety. The intention is not to explain away a difficult situation as simply a problem with your thinking.

## ACT connects awareness with practical choices.

[Acceptance and Commitment Therapy](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/) uses acceptance, mindfulness and action guided by values to develop psychological flexibility. This involves noticing what is happening internally while choosing how to respond to the situation in front of you. [ACBS introduces ACT for the public.](https://contextualscience.org/act_public)

In sessions, the work connects these ideas with a specific difficulty. What does worry ask you to do? What happens when you follow that demand? Which response would better reflect the person you want to be in that situation? Conversation and experiential practice help make those questions concrete.

For example, a goal might be participating more fully in a friendship rather than spending the whole time monitoring how you seem. Goals and any practice are individual. The work does not depend on a promise that anxious thoughts or feelings will never return.

## The approach should match the pattern.

Worry and intrusive thoughts can overlap. When repeated checking, reassurance-seeking or mental reviewing are central to the difficulty, it is important to understand whether an OCD-related cycle is involved. [OCD counselling at Unravel](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/) includes ERP, rather than treating every repeated thought as a general worry.

Where anxiety is connected with distressing experiences, [EMDR](https://unravelcounselling.com/emdr-therapy-bc/) may be considered as a secondary approach. ACT remains the main framework. Choosing an approach involves understanding your needs and circumstances, not selecting a therapy because its name sounds familiar.

A free consultation is an introduction to the practice, not a formal diagnostic assessment. Needs such as a diagnostic report, medication advice or a different level of care should be raised when enquiring so the scope of the service is clear.

Read [OCD versus anxiety](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/ocd-vs-anxiety/) for more on the overlap and why the pattern matters when choosing care.

## Counselling across BC, without travelling to a clinic.

Sessions with [Theekshitha Vadladi](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/) take place virtually. Adults aged 18 and over are welcome from Vancouver and elsewhere in British Columbia. Clients must be physically located in BC during care.

Privacy and a workable video connection matter. Before arranging sessions, consider where you would be able to speak and whether the format suits your circumstances. Appointment availability, session length and [fees](https://unravelcounselling.com/low-cost-counselling-bc/) are practical parts of choosing care.

Unravel has an understanding of South Asian and first-generation experiences and welcomes adults from all backgrounds. Culture, family, faith and belonging can be included without assuming that they mean the same thing for everyone.

## What the first steps involve.

### Explore the service

Use a free 15-minute phone or video consultation to ask about the approach, availability and practical arrangements.

### Understand your experience

Early sessions consider the situations, thoughts, feelings and responses affecting your day, alongside your goals and circumstances.

### Connect learning with daily life

Reflect on what is useful, try agreed practice where appropriate and review its effect. Your goals help determine what needs attention next.

## Fees and format

Free consultation: 15 minutes, phone or video. Individual session: CAD $145 for 50 minutes. Extended individual session: CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. Adults 18+, virtual, physically located in BC during sessions.

## Common questions

### Do I need an anxiety diagnosis to enquire?

No. Start with what you are noticing and the support you are seeking. The consultation covers fit and practical questions; it does not establish a diagnosis.

### What type of counselling does Unravel use for anxiety?

ACT is the main approach. OCD-related patterns may call for ERP, while EMDR can be considered for anxiety connected with distressing experiences. The role of each approach should be clear in your care.

### Is online anxiety counselling available outside Vancouver?

Yes. Adults elsewhere in British Columbia can attend virtually, provided they are physically located in BC during sessions.

### How many sessions will I need?

There is no set number promised. Goals, session frequency, affordability and the usefulness of the work are reviewed together. A consultation does not commit you to a package.

# ACT Therapy Vancouver & BC | Unravel Counselling

Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is Unravel’s main approach to virtual OCD and anxiety counselling for adults in British Columbia.

## More choice in how you respond.

Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, pronounced as the word “act”, is a behavioural therapy focused on psychological flexibility. In plain language, that means noticing the present situation and responding in ways that serve your values, even when difficult thoughts or feelings are present. [The Association for Contextual Behavioral Science explains ACT and its purpose.](https://contextualscience.org/act)

At Unravel, ACT informs work with anxiety and the wider framework for OCD counselling. It is used with adults aged 18 and over through virtual sessions in Vancouver and across British Columbia. Your circumstances give the work its meaning: the decisions, responsibilities and relationships you are trying to navigate.

## Six connected skills, explained simply.

ACT brings together six processes. They are connected ways of developing flexibility, rather than stages to pass or standards to perform perfectly. [ACBS describes the six core processes.](https://contextualscience.org/six_core_processes_act)

- Acceptance: willingness to experience a difficult feeling when doing so supports a meaningful action.
- Defusion: noticing a thought as an event in your mind rather than automatically following it as a rule.
- Present-moment awareness: directing attention to what is happening now, with flexibility to return when it wanders.
- Perspective: recognising that a difficult thought, feeling or label is part of your experience rather than the whole of who you are.
- Values: identifying the qualities you want to bring to the way you live and relate to others.
- Committed action: taking useful steps in those directions and adjusting in response to what you learn.

## What ACT can look like in a session.

A session may start with a specific moment: an avoided decision, a familiar worry or an interaction that did not go as you wanted. The focus is the relationship between what showed up internally, how you responded and what that response made possible or difficult.

The work can include conversation, an experiential exercise, a metaphor or a short practice in noticing thoughts and feelings. The purpose of an exercise should be clear. Language and examples need to fit the individual, rather than asking everyone to connect with the same metaphor.

For example, a person who values friendship might repeatedly decline invitations while waiting to feel entirely confident. ACT would explore the worry and the choice in relation to that value. The next step would be chosen in light of their needs, circumstances and what connection means to them.

Completed training: Acceptance & Commitment Therapy: 2-Day Intensive ACT Training, PESI, with Daniel J. Moran, PhD, BCBA-D.

## Values belong in the context of your life.

Values are qualities you want to express in how you live, rather than a list of outcomes you must achieve. They might concern care, honesty, connection, learning or another direction that has meaning for you. Your counsellor does not choose those priorities for you.

At Unravel, values work includes culture, family, faith, identity and responsibilities. It does not assume that independence is everyone’s central goal, or that connection with family prevents change. Commitments can be examined with respect for their meaning and their cost.

Acceptance concerns your relationship with internal experiences. It does not require approving every thought or accepting a harmful circumstance. Practical changes, boundaries and sources of support can still be part of the work. [The ACBS public introduction](https://contextualscience.org/act_public) describes ACT’s emphasis on values and flexible behaviour.

## How ACT relates to OCD-specific ERP.

For OCD, [Exposure and Response Prevention](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/) addresses the compulsive response within the cycle. ACT can support willingness, attention and the direction of the work. These are different roles, and the distinction matters when choosing OCD care.

The [IOCDF treatment guide](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/) identifies ERP as a first-line treatment and ACT as an adjunctive approach. At Unravel, the role of each approach is explained within a care plan that remains specific to the OCD cycle and your goals.

The [anxiety counselling page](https://unravelcounselling.com/anxiety-counselling-bc/) and [OCD therapy page](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/) explain how the practice approaches each concern. Theekshitha Vadladi’s education and completed courses are set out on the [counsellor profile](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/).

## From noticing a pattern to choosing a response.

### Clarify a direction

Identify the activities, relationships and qualities that matter in the context of your life.

### Understand what gets in the way

Notice thoughts, feelings, urges and familiar responses, including the short- and longer-term effects of those responses.

### Try and review

Choose an individual next step, reflect on what happens and adjust the work in relation to your goals.

## Fees and format

Free consultation: 15 minutes, phone or video. Individual session: CAD $145 for 50 minutes. Extended individual session: CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. Adults 18+, virtual, physically located in BC during sessions.

## Common questions

### Does acceptance mean agreeing with a thought?

No. In ACT, acceptance concerns willingness to experience what happens internally. It does not require believing every thought, following every urge or approving a harmful situation.

### Will ACT stop anxious thoughts?

ACT does not promise that difficult thoughts will disappear. It focuses on developing a more flexible relationship with them and choosing responses linked to your values.

### Do I need to know how to meditate?

No meditation background is required. Mindful attention is introduced in relation to the work, and exercises can be explained in ordinary language.

### Is ACT counselling offered online across BC?

Yes. Unravel offers individual virtual counselling to adults aged 18 and over in Vancouver and throughout British Columbia. Clients must be physically in BC during sessions.

## Where to next

- [Anxiety counselling](https://unravelcounselling.com/anxiety-counselling-bc/)
- [OCD counselling](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/)
- [ERP and response prevention](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/)

# Online EMDR Therapy Vancouver | Unravel Counselling

Virtual EMDR counselling for adults in Vancouver and BC, considered as a secondary approach for anxiety and trauma where appropriate.

## Understanding the approach before beginning memory work.

Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing, or EMDR, is a structured psychotherapy that works with distress associated with memories and experiences. The process includes understanding your history, preparation, guided processing and review. Eye movements, taps or tones may be used as part of the wider approach; they are not the whole therapy.

Clinical guidelines most clearly support EMDR in PTSD care. The [NICE PTSD recommendations](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng116/chapter/recommendations) describe a phased treatment delivered by trained practitioners. At Unravel, EMDR is offered for anxiety and trauma where appropriate, without assuming that every anxiety concern calls for memory processing.

## Start with what is affecting life now.

A difficult experience may continue to influence how a situation feels in the present. For example, someone might notice distress connected with a reminder of an earlier event. That observation is a starting point for understanding the concern, not proof that EMDR is the appropriate treatment.

ACT remains Unravel’s main approach. EMDR is considered as a secondary method for anxiety and trauma, in relation to the person’s needs and circumstances. Choosing a therapy involves more than matching a symptom with a technique.

OCD counselling at Unravel uses [ERP](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/). A history of difficult experiences does not automatically make EMDR the appropriate approach to an OCD cycle. Where concerns overlap, the purpose and focus of the work need to be clear.

## Preparation is a substantive part of EMDR.

EMDR involves more than recalling something upsetting while following eye movements. History-taking and preparation help establish what is being addressed, the person’s current circumstances and what is needed before processing. Later work includes closing the session and reviewing what follows.

Questions about readiness, pacing, pauses and managing distress belong in that preparation. Memory processing is not a step that everyone is promised in a first appointment, and there is no universal timetable for reaching it. Preparation, collaboration and informed choices guide the process.

The [EMDR International Association introduces the therapy and its trauma focus](https://www.emdria.org/about-emdr-therapy/). General descriptions are useful background, but they cannot determine an individual treatment plan. Your understanding of the proposed work matters throughout the process.

## The online setting needs to support the work.

Unravel offers virtual sessions for adults aged 18 and over who are physically located in British Columbia, including Vancouver. A private setting, suitable device and workable internet connection are important practical considerations.

For memory-focused work, the setting deserves particular attention. Consider whether you can speak privately, what interruptions may occur and whether the online format suits your circumstances. Questions about the connection and how appointments end should be clarified before beginning.

If the setting or your current needs make virtual memory work difficult, that information is relevant to choosing care. The consultation provides an introduction to the service; it does not commit you to processing a particular memory or choosing EMDR.

## Clear information about your counsellor’s training.

EMDR at Unravel is offered by [Theekshitha Vadladi](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/). She has completed both parts of her EMDRIA-approved basic training and the required consultation. The counsellor profile provides the course, provider and trainer details alongside her completed education.

Basic training and EMDRIA certification are distinct. The [EMDRIA training and certification guide](https://www.emdria.org/training-vs-certification/) explains that completing basic training does not itself confer certification.

The working relationship also matters. Clear explanations, respect for your circumstances and attention to your choices are part of considering care. Cultural context and values remain relevant whichever approach is being used.

Completed training: EMDR Basic Training, EMDR Training Associates, with Alivia Maric and Eve Wilensky. Both training parts and required consultation are complete.

## A phased approach, with preparation and review.

### Understand the concern

Explore the present difficulty, relevant history and what you want help to change. Clarify the role being proposed for EMDR.

### Prepare for the work

Consider readiness, resources, expectations and the online setting before deciding on memory processing.

### Continue and review

Where EMDR is appropriate, proceed with guided work, session closure and review of what follows. The plan remains individual.

## Fees and format

Free consultation: 15 minutes, phone or video. Individual session: CAD $145 for 50 minutes. Extended individual session: CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. Adults 18+, virtual, physically located in BC during sessions.

## Common questions

### Does EMDR begin with memory processing in the first session?

EMDR begins with understanding your needs and preparing for the work. Readiness and pacing help determine when memory processing is appropriate.

### Do I need to describe every detail in the consultation?

No. The free 15-minute phone or video consultation is an introduction focused on practical questions and fit. You do not need to provide a detailed account of a distressing experience to enquire.

### What does EMDR counselling cost?

Individual sessions are CAD $145 for 50 minutes or CAD $190 for 90 minutes. The appropriate session option is considered in relation to the work. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. See [fees and session details](https://unravelcounselling.com/low-cost-counselling-bc/).

### Is EMDR covered by insurance?

Coverage depends on your insurance plan and its provider requirements. Confirm eligibility directly with your insurer before booking paid sessions. See [fees and insurance information](https://unravelcounselling.com/low-cost-counselling-bc/).

## Where to next

# Mental Compulsions in OCD: The Rituals You Cannot See

Someone can look still while spending hours reviewing, checking or trying to undo a thought. Understanding the purpose of that thinking helps explain mental compulsions.

By [Theekshitha Vadladi](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)

Published: 2026-11-03

General information to support a conversation about care. This article does not diagnose your experience or provide an individual treatment plan.

## What is a mental compulsion?

A mental compulsion is a repeated internal act performed in response to an obsession or a rule someone feels driven to follow. It may aim to reduce distress, prevent a feared outcome or reach a feeling of certainty. The ritual happens in thought, so it can be difficult for other people to notice.

In OCD, a person may repeatedly reconstruct a conversation, count silently, replace an unwanted thought with another thought, or check whether a feeling is present. What matters is the role the response plays in the pattern. Remembering an event or repeating a phrase is not automatically a compulsion.

Sources: [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/); [NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over).

## Examples of rituals that happen internally

Consider someone who remembers a conversation and worries that a comment revealed something terrible about them. They replay the wording, inspect their intentions and search their memory for a detail that would settle the concern. An answer briefly feels convincing, until another possible interpretation appears.

That example illustrates a possible OCD cycle, rather than a way to identify OCD from one situation. Internal responses can take different forms, including:

- Mental reviewing: replaying events or conversations to resolve doubt.
- Neutralising: using a thought, image or phrase to try to cancel another one.
- Internal checking: repeatedly inspecting feelings, intentions or bodily reactions.
- Counting or repeating: following an internal sequence until a rule or feeling of completeness is met.

Sources: [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/); [IOCDF: Understanding compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/).

## Why the answer may never feel finished

A ritual may bring short-lived relief. The problem is that the next doubt can call for another round, and the demand for certainty grows harder to satisfy. Time and attention become organised around answering the concern instead of taking part in the day.

This helps explain why more reasoning does not always feel useful. The issue may be the repeated attempt to obtain certainty, rather than a missing piece of information. Compulsive reviewing can also occur after a visible ritual or an exposure, so the full sequence deserves attention.

Sources: [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/); [IOCDF: Understanding compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/).

- [Read about rumination in OCD](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/rumination-ocd/)

## Ordinary reflection and valued practices need context

People think carefully about mistakes, reflect on relationships and use repeated words in meaningful ways. Prayer, for example, can be an important religious practice. Its form alone cannot tell us whether a compulsive process is involved.

A useful clinical conversation considers the purpose, rigidity, distress and effect on life. Faith and cultural commitments deserve respectful understanding. It also matters whether trying to classify every thought as a ritual has itself become another time-consuming search for certainty.

Sources: [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/); [IOCDF: OCD and scrupulosity](https://iocdf.org/faith-ocd/what-is-ocd-scrupulosity/).

- [Explore common OCD themes](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-types/)

## How ERP includes mental rituals

Exposure and Response Prevention is a form of cognitive behavioural therapy used for OCD. Exposure involves planned contact with a trigger; response prevention addresses the ritual that usually follows. When the ritual is mental, that internal response belongs in the plan.

Response prevention does not require an empty mind. A thought appearing and the effort to neutralise or repeatedly resolve it are different parts of the experience. Understanding that distinction helps identify what is being practised. The starting point and pace need to be planned for the individual.

At Unravel, ACT is the main framework and ERP is used for OCD. ACT supports willingness, attention and action guided by values alongside the OCD-specific work. The purpose is connected with the life the rituals are interrupting.

Sources: [IOCDF: Exposure and Response Prevention](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/); [ACBS: The six core processes of ACT](https://contextualscience.org/six_core_processes_act).

- [How ERP works](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/)
- [ACT at Unravel](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/)

## What to bring to a first conversation

A broad description is enough to begin: what tends to trigger the loop, what you feel driven to do mentally and how much it interrupts your day. Questions about training, mental rituals and the proposed approach can help you consider whether a service is appropriate.

Unravel offers virtual individual OCD counselling for adults aged 18 and over who are physically in British Columbia, including Vancouver. A free 15-minute phone or video consultation covers the approach, fees and availability.

- [Explore online OCD counselling](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/)
- [Meet Theekshitha Vadladi](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)

- [Blog and resources](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/)
- [Meet the author](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)
- [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/)
- [IOCDF: Understanding compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/)
- [NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over)
- [IOCDF: OCD and scrupulosity](https://iocdf.org/faith-ocd/what-is-ocd-scrupulosity/)
- [IOCDF: Exposure and Response Prevention](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/)
- [ACBS: The six core processes of ACT](https://contextualscience.org/six_core_processes_act)

# Rumination and OCD: When Thinking Becomes a Ritual

One more replay, one more explanation, one more attempt to be sure. Rumination can feel like problem-solving while keeping the original doubt open.

By [Theekshitha Vadladi](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)

Published: 2026-11-03

General information to support a conversation about care. This article does not diagnose your experience or provide an individual treatment plan.

## Can rumination be an OCD compulsion?

Yes. Repeated reasoning or mental reviewing can function as a compulsion when it is used to resolve an obsessional doubt. The thinking may concern a past event, a relationship, morality or another subject that feels urgent to settle.

Rumination also occurs outside OCD. Its presence does not establish a diagnosis. To understand it, a clinical conversation looks at what sets it off, the response it calls for and the effect on a person’s life, rather than relying on the topic alone.

Sources: [IOCDF: Compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/); [Ghaznavi, Schiewe and Stern: Management of rumination and obsessions in primary care](https://www.psychiatrist.com/pcc/management-rumination-obsessions-primary-care/).

## The answer that keeps needing another answer

Imagine reviewing an email because you worry that it sounded unkind. You reconstruct why you chose each word, compare possible interpretations and consider what the recipient might think. For a moment, one explanation seems sufficient. Then a different possibility pulls you back into the review.

The difficulty is not necessarily a lack of effort. The person may be working intensely to solve the concern. But a process organised around complete certainty can keep reopening a question whenever another possibility appears. Meanwhile, rest, work or a conversation happening in the present becomes harder to return to.

Sources: [IOCDF: Compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/).

## Reflection usually has a practical purpose

Looking back on an experience can help someone understand what happened, decide whether an action is needed or learn for next time. Compulsive reviewing may keep searching after the available information has already been considered, because the stopping point depends on feeling certain.

This is a distinction to explore with care, not a rule for policing every thought. A rigid effort to decide whether each moment of thinking is healthy reflection or rumination can itself become another loop. Context, function and the wider pattern matter.

The question is also broader than whether the event was real. OCD-related doubt can concern an actual experience, an imagined possibility or uncertainty about memory. A label such as real-event or false-memory OCD does not establish what happened.

Sources: [IOCDF: Compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/); [Ghaznavi, Schiewe and Stern: Management of rumination and obsessions in primary care](https://www.psychiatrist.com/pcc/management-rumination-obsessions-primary-care/).

- [OCD themes and memory-related doubt](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-types/)

## Why reassurance may become part of the loop

Reviewing sometimes moves between internal analysis and asking another person to confirm an interpretation. Searching online can serve a similar purpose. A reply may settle one version of the concern while leaving room for another question.

The relevant issue is how the response functions. Asking for information or support is part of ordinary life; repeated attempts to obtain certainty may be relevant to an OCD care plan. The full sequence can include less visible responses that happen after the conversation ends.

Sources: [IOCDF: Compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/).

- [Mental compulsions explained](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/mental-compulsions-ocd/)

## How ERP and ACT approach the pattern

ERP combines planned contact with OCD triggers and practice changing compulsive responses. If repeated mental review follows a trigger, response prevention needs to account for it. The work is more specific than trying to think positively or distracting yourself until the question goes away.

At Unravel, ACT provides the main therapeutic framework, with ERP for OCD. ACT brings attention to psychological flexibility and chosen values. A goal might involve being more present with a friend or completing a task without giving the rest of the evening to review.

Practice is selected collaboratively and reviewed in relation to the individual pattern. An educational article cannot determine the right starting point, the relevant mental ritual or the pace for someone it has never met.

Sources: [IOCDF: Exposure and Response Prevention](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/); [ACBS: The six core processes of ACT](https://contextualscience.org/six_core_processes_act).

- [Exposure and Response Prevention](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/)
- [Acceptance and Commitment Therapy](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/)

## Asking for help while the doubt is unfinished

A first conversation can begin with the loop and its cost. It does not require a final answer to the original question. Ask how the counsellor identifies mental rituals, plans response prevention and reviews the effect on daily life.

Unravel offers online OCD and anxiety counselling for adults physically located in BC, including Vancouver. A free 15-minute phone or video consultation is available for questions about the approach, fees and current availability.

- [OCD counselling at Unravel](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/)
- [Consultation details](https://unravelcounselling.com/contact/)

- [Blog and resources](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/)
- [Meet the author](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)
- [IOCDF: Compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/)
- [Ghaznavi, Schiewe and Stern: Management of rumination and obsessions in primary care](https://www.psychiatrist.com/pcc/management-rumination-obsessions-primary-care/)
- [IOCDF: Exposure and Response Prevention](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/)

# OCD vs Anxiety: Why the Pattern Matters

Anxiety can occur within OCD and alongside it. Looking at what happens after a thought appears helps explain why the distinction matters for treatment.

By [Theekshitha Vadladi](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)

Published: 2026-11-03

General information to support a conversation about care. This article does not diagnose your experience or provide an individual treatment plan.

## What is the difference between OCD and anxiety?

Anxiety is a feeling that can occur in ordinary life and in several mental health conditions. OCD is characterised by obsessions, compulsions or both, with significant distress or interference. Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) involves persistent, difficult-to-control worry across areas of life.

These descriptions overlap in experience. A person can feel anxious because of an OCD obsession, and OCD can occur alongside an anxiety disorder. “OCD or anxiety?” is therefore not always an either-or question.

Sources: [NIMH: Generalized anxiety disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/generalized-anxiety-disorder-gad); [NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over).

## In OCD, the response to doubt needs attention

Obsessions can be unwanted thoughts, images or urges. Compulsions are repetitive behaviours or mental acts that someone feels driven to carry out, often to reduce distress or prevent a feared outcome. Checking, washing, repeated reassurance-seeking and mental reviewing can be part of the pattern.

A person may appear calm while performing internal rituals. The relevant questions include what triggers the response, what it is intended to achieve and how it affects daily life. Having an upsetting thought or preferring order does not, by itself, establish OCD.

Sources: [NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over); [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/).

- [Mental compulsions in OCD](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/mental-compulsions-ocd/)
- [OCD counselling](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/)

## Persistent worry can spread across daily life

In GAD, worry may concern work, health, finances, family or several areas at once. Feeling on edge, tension, poor sleep and difficulty concentrating may accompany it. Duration, frequency, impact and the wider health picture matter to assessment.

Anxiety counselling can begin with the experience rather than a label: the decisions you avoid, the preparation that never feels sufficient, or the effort it takes to get through the day. Real pressures such as financial strain and discrimination belong in that understanding too.

Sources: [NIMH: Generalized anxiety disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/generalized-anxiety-disorder-gad).

- [Anxiety counselling at Unravel](https://unravelcounselling.com/anxiety-counselling-bc/)

## Realistic concerns and intrusive thoughts can overlap

The subject of a thought does not reliably settle the distinction. Health, family and responsibility can appear in ordinary worry, OCD and other difficulties. A thought about a real concern does not automatically rule OCD out, and an unusual thought does not automatically establish it.

For example, reviewing an email might support a practical correction in one situation. In another, it might become a repeated attempt to settle an obsessional doubt. The action can look similar while its function and place in the wider pattern differ.

This is why symptom comparisons can only go so far. If repeated searches for the right diagnosis have themselves become time-consuming, that experience is relevant to bring into a clinical conversation.

Sources: [NIMH: Generalized anxiety disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/generalized-anxiety-disorder-gad); [NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over); [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/).

## Why the distinction changes the treatment discussion

ERP is a first-line psychological treatment for OCD. It combines planned contact with triggers and practice changing compulsive responses, including mental rituals. A plan that overlooks the rituals may miss an important part of the difficulty.

At Unravel, ACT is the main framework for counselling, with ERP used for OCD. ACT supports awareness, psychological flexibility and actions guided by values. In anxiety care, the work considers responses to worry and avoidance in relation to the person’s needs and circumstances.

The role of a method should be clear. Asking how a proposed approach addresses your particular pattern is more useful than selecting a therapy solely because its name is familiar.

Sources: [IOCDF: Exposure and Response Prevention](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/); [ACBS: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy](https://contextualscience.org/act).

- [ERP for OCD](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/)
- [ACT and psychological flexibility](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/)

## Where to begin if you are unsure

Describe what happens, what you feel driven to do next and what the pattern interrupts. Ask about the practice’s scope, the counsellor’s training and whether another assessment would be useful. If you need a formal diagnosis or report, raise that need when enquiring.

Unravel offers virtual individual counselling for adults aged 18 and over who are physically located in British Columbia, including Vancouver. The free 15-minute phone or video consultation covers fit and practical questions; it is not a formal diagnostic assessment.

- [Education and training](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)
- [Fees and consultation options](https://unravelcounselling.com/low-cost-counselling-bc/)

- [Blog and resources](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/)
- [Meet the author](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)
- [NIMH: Generalized anxiety disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/generalized-anxiety-disorder-gad)
- [NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over)
- [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/)
